-- the file's smpl chunk defines, it is applied from our own header probe.
local function load_file_into_sample(smp, path, info)
  pcall(function() smp.loop_mode = 1 end)  -- no stale loop from before
  local loaded = smp.sample_buffer:load_from(path)
  if loaded == false or not smp.sample_buffer.has_sample_data then
    error("could not read " .. basename(path), 0)
  end
  info = info or probe_file(path)
  pcall(function()
    local n = smp.sample_buffer.number_of_frames
    if prefs.file_loops.value then
      if info and info.loop and smp.loop_mode == 1 then
        local s = clamp(info.loop.start, 1, n)
        local e = clamp(info.loop.stop, s, n)
        smp.loop_mode = info.loop.mode
        smp.loop_end = n
        smp.loop_start = s
        smp.loop_end = e
      end
    else
      smp.loop_mode = 1
    end
    if smp.loop_mode == 1 and prefs.default_loop.value > 1 then
      smp.loop_start = 1
      smp.loop_end = n
      smp.loop_mode = clamp(prefs.default_loop.value, 1, 4)
    end
  end)
  pcall(function()
    smp.interpolation_mode = clamp(prefs.default_interp.value, 1, 4)
  end)
end

-- Beats a looping sample should span at the song tempo, or nil.
-- Uses a BPM in the file name ("loop_120bpm.wav") when there is one,
-- otherwise the power of two beats closest to the song tempo.
local function sync_beats(smp, path)
  if not prefs.sync_tempo.value then return nil end
  local buf = smp.sample_buffer
  local secs = buf.number_of_frames / math.max(1, buf.sample_rate)
  if secs < 0.05 then return nil end
  local named = tonumber((basename(path or ""):lower()
                          :match("(%d%d%d?)%s*_?bpm")))
  if named and named >= 40 and named <= 300 then
    return math.max(1, math.floor(secs * named / 60 + 0.5))
  end
  local bpm = renoise.song().transport.bpm
  -- one-shots shorter than about a beat are never stretched
  if smp.loop_mode == 1 and secs < 0.9 * 60 / bpm then return nil end
  local best, best_err
  for _, n in ipairs { 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 } do
    local err = math.abs(math.log((n * 60 / secs) / bpm))
    if not best_err or err < best_err then best, best_err = n, err end
  end
  if best_err > math.log(1.5) then return nil end
  return best
end

-- Apply the browser's Beatsync setting to a sample. Used for the preview
-- and for everything that gets loaded, so what you hear is what you get.
local function apply_browser_settings(smp, path)
  pcall(function()
    local beats = sync_beats(smp, path)
    if beats then
      smp.beat_sync_lines = clamp(beats * renoise.song().transport.lpb, 1, 512)
      pcall(function() smp.beat_sync_mode = clamp(prefs.sync_mode.value, 1, 3) end)
      smp.beat_sync_enabled = true

    end
  end)
end

-- put a sample's loop exactly there (kept inside the sample)
function C.put_loop(smp, mode, ls, le)
  local n = smp.sample_buffer.number_of_frames
  ls = clamp(math.floor(ls), 1, n)
  le = clamp(math.floor(le), ls, n)
  smp.loop_mode = 1
  smp.loop_start = 1
  smp.loop_end = le
  smp.loop_start = ls
  smp.loop_mode = clamp(mode, 1, 4)
end

-- trim to / cut out frames a..b of a sample's audio (the loop moves along)
function C.edit_data(smp, mode, a, b)
  local buf = smp.sample_buffer
  local n, chs = buf.number_of_frames, buf.number_of_channels
  a, b = clamp(a, 1, n), clamp(b, 1, n)
  local keep = (mode == "trim") and { { a, b } } or { { 1, a - 1 }, { b + 1, n } }
  local total = 0
  for _, k in ipairs(keep) do total = total + math.max(0, k[2] - k[1] + 1) end
  if total < 2 then error("nothing would be left", 0) end
  -- where a frame of the old sample ends up
  local function moved(f)
    if mode == "trim" then return clamp(f - a + 1, 1, total) end
    if f < a then return f end
    if f > b then return f - (b - a + 1) end
    return clamp(a, 1, total)
  end
  local data = {}
  for c = 1, chs do
    local t, i = {}, 0
    for _, k in ipairs(keep) do
      for f = k[1], k[2] do i = i + 1 t[i] = buf:sample_data(c, f) end
    end
    data[c] = t
  end
  local rate, bits = buf.sample_rate, buf.bit_depth
  local lm, ls, le = smp.loop_mode, smp.loop_start, smp.loop_end
  local interp = smp.interpolation_mode
  if not buf:create_sample_data(rate, bits, chs, total) then
    error("could not make the new sample", 0)
  end
  buf:prepare_sample_data_changes(false)   -- the preview needs no undo
  for c = 1, chs do
    local t = data[c]
    for f = 1, total do buf:set_sample_data(c, f, t[f]) end
  end
  buf:finalize_sample_data_changes()
  local nls, nle = moved(ls), moved(le)
  C.put_loop(smp, nle > nls and lm or 1, nls, math.max(nls, nle))
  pcall(function() smp.interpolation_mode = interp end)
end

-- equal-power crossfade over `len` frames at the loop (see below)
function C.xfade_data(smp, len)
  local buf = smp.sample_buffer
  local ls, le = smp.loop_start, smp.loop_end
  len = math.min(len, ls - 1, le - ls)
  if len < 2 then error("needs audio before the loop start", 0) end
  local half_pi = math.pi / 2
  local sin, cos = math.sin, math.cos
  buf:prepare_sample_data_changes(false)
  for c = 1, buf.number_of_channels do
    for k = 1, len do
      local t = k / len
      local dst = le - len + k            -- end of the loop, fading out
      local src = ls - len + k - 1        -- before the start, fading in
      buf:set_sample_data(c, dst,
        buf:sample_data(c, dst) * cos(t * half_pi)
        + buf:sample_data(c, src) * sin(t * half_pi))
    end
  end
  buf:finalize_sample_data_changes()
end

-- one step on a sample
function C.apply_op(smp, op)
  if op.t == "loop" then C.put_loop(smp, op.mode, op.s, op.e)
  elseif op.t == "interp" then smp.interpolation_mode = clamp(op.mode, 1, 4)
  elseif op.t == "trim" or op.t == "cut" then C.edit_data(smp, op.t, op.a, op.b)
  elseif op.t == "xfade" then
    if op.ls then C.put_loop(smp, op.mode, op.ls, op.le) end  -- its loop
    C.xfade_data(smp, op.len)
  end
end

-- the loop of a sample as a step
function C.loop_op(smp)
  return { t = "loop", mode = smp.loop_mode, s = smp.loop_start, e = smp.loop_end }

function C.edit_preview(mode)
  C.quiet()
  local r = S.sel_range
  local smp = C.preview_smp()
  if not r or not smp then
    set_status("Drag across the waveform to select a part first")
    return
  end
  release_all()
  clear_preview_slices()
  local op = { t = mode, a = r[1], b = r[2] }
  local ok, err = pcall(C.apply_op, smp, op)
  if not ok then
    set_status("Edit failed: " .. tostring(err))
    return
  end
  S.sel_range = nil
  C.record({ op }, mode == "trim" and "Trim" or "Cut")
  C.preview_changed(true)
  set_status((mode == "trim" and "Trimmed" or "Cut") .. " the preview copy"
             .. " - loading it now uses this version (the file is untouched)")
end

-- back to the file as it is: all its steps go (one undo brings them back)
function C.undo_edits()
  local p = S.loaded_path
  local list = p and C.ops_of(p)
  if not list or #list == 0 then
    set_status("This sample has no changes")
    return
  end
  local saved = {}
  for i, op in ipairs(list) do saved[i] = op end
  local function clear() S.ops[C.file_key(p)] = {} C.reload_preview(p) end
  clear()
  C.push_undo {
    name = "Back to the file", path = p, preview = true,
    undo = function()
      local l = {}
      for i, op in ipairs(saved) do l[i] = op end
      S.ops[C.file_key(p)] = l
      C.reload_preview(p)
    end,
    redo = clear,
  }
  set_status("Back to the file as it is")
end

-- What to load for `path`: the file, or the edited copy (saved now) after
-- a trim / cut / crossfade; plus the loop and interpolation to give it
-- (nil: the defaults). A file with changes that is not in the preview is
-- put there first, so its steps are replayed.
function C.source_for(path)
  local list = C.ops_of(path)
  local here = same_path(path, S.loaded_path) and not S.wave_from_kit
  if not here and not (list and #list > 0) then return path, false, nil end
  if not here and not load_preview(path) then return path, false, nil end
  local smp = scratch_sample()
  if not smp then return path, false, nil end
  local props = { loop = C.loop_op(smp), interp = smp.interpolation_mode }
  if S.edited then
    if not (S.edit_tmp and io.exists(S.edit_tmp)) then
      local dir = C.edits_dir()
      pcall(function() if not dir_exists(dir) then os.mkdir(dir) end end)
      C.edit_n = (C.edit_n or 0) + 1
      local f = join(dir, string.format("%s (edit %d).wav",
        stem(path):gsub("[^%w%-_ %.%(%)]", "_"), C.edit_n))
      local ok = pcall(function()
        return smp.sample_buffer:save_as(f, "wav")
      end)
      if ok and io.exists(f) then S.edit_tmp = f end
    end
    if S.edit_tmp then return S.edit_tmp, true, props end
  end
  return path, false, props
end

-- give a loaded sample the loop and interpolation from C.source_for
function C.apply_props(smp, props)
  if not props then return end
  pcall(function()
    local l = props.loop
    if l then C.put_loop(smp, l.mode, l.s, l.e) end
    if props.interp then smp.interpolation_mode = props.interp end
  end)
end

-- PakettiLoadSampleBrowser.lua
-- Impulse Tracker "Load Sample" screen for Renoise: a Canvas file browser that
-- lets you navigate folders, see a highlighted file's metadata + waveform, and
-- KEYJAZZ the file on the qwerty piano keyboard WITHOUT loading it into your song.
--
-- How the "loadless preview" works: highlighting a file loads it into a single
-- hidden scratch instrument (created at the end of the instrument list). The piano
-- keys trigger that scratch instrument via trigger_instrument_note_on, so you hear
-- the file during playback without disturbing your song. Nothing touches your real
-- instruments until you CONFIRM (Enter, or press the toggle shortcut again), which
-- loads the file fresh into the smart target slot with the Paketti default template
-- and returns you to the Pattern Editor. Esc cancels and deletes the scratch
-- instrument, leaving no residue.
--
-- Keys in dialog:
--   Up/Down         move the file cursor (loads the highlighted file for preview)
--   Mod+Up/Down     any modifier (Cmd/Option/Shift/Ctrl) + Up/Down jumps to top/bottom
--   PageUp/PageDown jump a screenful
--   Enter / Return  on a folder: enter it; on a file: LOAD into target + return to Pattern Editor
--   Backspace / Left go up to the parent folder; from a Windows drive root (C:\) this
--                   goes up to a synthetic "Drives" list to hop between C:/D:/E: etc.
--   Open Folder…    button: native folder picker, reaches any folder/drive (C:/D:/E:, network)
--   Esc             cancel + unload (delete scratch instrument)
--   F1-F12          jump to folder preset N; Shift+F1-F12 stores the current folder as preset N
--   Right-Shift     "load and jam": load into the smart target slot (selected-if-empty,
--                   else first empty, else new), select it, close, turn on Edit Mode +
--                   Follow Pattern, jump to the Pattern Editor
--   Piano keys      keyjazz the highlighted file (zsxdcvgbhnjm + 23 567 9 + qwertyuiop)
--   < / >           lower / raise the keyboard (transport) octave for keyjazz
--   Space           passes through to Renoise transport (start/stop during audition)
--   Shift+Enter     load all sample files directly inside the selected folder
--   < / >           pass through to Renoise octave controls
--   Toggle shortcut confirms + closes through the same deferred action as Enter.
--
-- The folder you are in is remembered (and becomes the default next time); if it has
-- since been deleted it reverts to ~/Music/Samples. The first time you ever open the
-- dialog it asks you to pick a default folder. The highlighted file is remembered too,
-- so reopening lands you back where you were (clamped if the folder now has fewer files).

-- the file's smpl chunk defines, it is applied from our own header probe.
local function load_file_into_sample(smp, path, info)
  pcall(function() smp.loop_mode = 1 end)  -- no stale loop from before
  local loaded = smp.sample_buffer:load_from(path)
  if loaded == false or not smp.sample_buffer.has_sample_data then
    error("could not read " .. basename(path), 0)
  end
  info = info or probe_file(path)
  pcall(function()
    local n = smp.sample_buffer.number_of_frames
    if prefs.file_loops.value then
      if info and info.loop and smp.loop_mode == 1 then
        local s = clamp(info.loop.start, 1, n)
        local e = clamp(info.loop.stop, s, n)
        smp.loop_mode = info.loop.mode
        smp.loop_end = n
        smp.loop_start = s
        smp.loop_end = e
      end
    else
      smp.loop_mode = 1
    end
    if smp.loop_mode == 1 and prefs.default_loop.value > 1 then
      smp.loop_start = 1
      smp.loop_end = n
      smp.loop_mode = clamp(prefs.default_loop.value, 1, 4)
    end
  end)
  pcall(function()
    smp.interpolation_mode = clamp(prefs.default_interp.value, 1, 4)
  end)
end

-- Beats a looping sample should span at the song tempo, or nil.
-- Uses a BPM in the file name ("loop_120bpm.wav") when there is one,
-- otherwise the power of two beats closest to the song tempo.
local function sync_beats(smp, path)
  if not prefs.sync_tempo.value then return nil end
  local buf = smp.sample_buffer
  local secs = buf.number_of_frames / math.max(1, buf.sample_rate)
  if secs < 0.05 then return nil end
  local named = tonumber((basename(path or ""):lower()
                          :match("(%d%d%d?)%s*_?bpm")))
  if named and named >= 40 and named <= 300 then
    return math.max(1, math.floor(secs * named / 60 + 0.5))
  end
  local bpm = renoise.song().transport.bpm
  -- one-shots shorter than about a beat are never stretched
  if smp.loop_mode == 1 and secs < 0.9 * 60 / bpm then return nil end
  local best, best_err
  for _, n in ipairs { 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 } do
    local err = math.abs(math.log((n * 60 / secs) / bpm))
    if not best_err or err < best_err then best, best_err = n, err end
  end
  if best_err > math.log(1.5) then return nil end
  return best
end

-- Apply the browser's Beatsync setting to a sample. Used for the preview
-- and for everything that gets loaded, so what you hear is what you get.
local function apply_browser_settings(smp, path)
  pcall(function()
    local beats = sync_beats(smp, path)
    if beats then
      smp.beat_sync_lines = clamp(beats * renoise.song().transport.lpb, 1, 512)
      pcall(function() smp.beat_sync_mode = clamp(prefs.sync_mode.value, 1, 3) end)
      smp.beat_sync_enabled = true
    else
      smp.beat_sync_enabled = false
    end
  end)
end

-- put a sample's loop exactly there (kept inside the sample)
function C.put_loop(smp, mode, ls, le)
  local n = smp.sample_buffer.number_of_frames
  ls = clamp(math.floor(ls), 1, n)
  le = clamp(math.floor(le), ls, n)
  smp.loop_mode = 1
  smp.loop_start = 1
  smp.loop_end = le
  smp.loop_start = ls
  smp.loop_mode = clamp(mode, 1, 4)
end

-- trim to / cut out frames a..b of a sample's audio (the loop moves along)
function C.edit_data(smp, mode, a, b)
  local buf = smp.sample_buffer
  local n, chs = buf.number_of_frames, buf.number_of_channels
  a, b = clamp(a, 1, n), clamp(b, 1, n)
  local keep = (mode == "trim") and { { a, b } } or { { 1, a - 1 }, { b + 1, n } }
  local total = 0
  for _, k in ipairs(keep) do total = total + math.max(0, k[2] - k[1] + 1) end
  if total < 2 then error("nothing would be left", 0) end
  -- where a frame of the old sample ends up
  local function moved(f)
    if mode == "trim" then return clamp(f - a + 1, 1, total) end
    if f < a then return f end
    if f > b then return f - (b - a + 1) end
    return clamp(a, 1, total)
  end
  local data = {}
  for c = 1, chs do
    local t, i = {}, 0
    for _, k in ipairs(keep) do
      for f = k[1], k[2] do i = i + 1 t[i] = buf:sample_data(c, f) end
    end
    data[c] = t
  end
  local rate, bits = buf.sample_rate, buf.bit_depth
  local lm, ls, le = smp.loop_mode, smp.loop_start, smp.loop_end
  local interp = smp.interpolation_mode
  if not buf:create_sample_data(rate, bits, chs, total) then
    error("could not make the new sample", 0)
  end
  buf:prepare_sample_data_changes(false)   -- the preview needs no undo
  for c = 1, chs do
    local t = data[c]
    for f = 1, total do buf:set_sample_data(c, f, t[f]) end
  end
  buf:finalize_sample_data_changes()
  local nls, nle = moved(ls), moved(le)
  C.put_loop(smp, nle > nls and lm or 1, nls, math.max(nls, nle))
  pcall(function() smp.interpolation_mode = interp end)
end

-- equal-power crossfade over `len` frames at the loop (see below)
function C.xfade_data(smp, len)
  local buf = smp.sample_buffer
  local ls, le = smp.loop_start, smp.loop_end
  len = math.min(len, ls - 1, le - ls)
  if len < 2 then error("needs audio before the loop start", 0) end
  local half_pi = math.pi / 2
  local sin, cos = math.sin, math.cos
  buf:prepare_sample_data_changes(false)
  for c = 1, buf.number_of_channels do
    for k = 1, len do
      local t = k / len
      local dst = le - len + k            -- end of the loop, fading out
      local src = ls - len + k - 1        -- before the start, fading in
      buf:set_sample_data(c, dst,
        buf:sample_data(c, dst) * cos(t * half_pi)
        + buf:sample_data(c, src) * sin(t * half_pi))
    end
  end
  buf:finalize_sample_data_changes()
end

-- one step on a sample
function C.apply_op(smp, op)
  if op.t == "loop" then C.put_loop(smp, op.mode, op.s, op.e)
  elseif op.t == "interp" then smp.interpolation_mode = clamp(op.mode, 1, 4)
  elseif op.t == "trim" or op.t == "cut" then C.edit_data(smp, op.t, op.a, op.b)
  elseif op.t == "xfade" then
    if op.ls then C.put_loop(smp, op.mode, op.ls, op.le) end  -- its loop
    C.xfade_data(smp, op.len)
  end
end

-- the loop of a sample as a step
function C.loop_op(smp)
  return { t = "loop", mode = smp.loop_mode, s = smp.loop_start, e = smp.loop_end }

function C.edit_preview(mode)
  C.quiet()
  local r = S.sel_range
  local smp = C.preview_smp()
  if not r or not smp then
    set_status("Drag across the waveform to select a part first")
    return
  end
  release_all()
  clear_preview_slices()
  local op = { t = mode, a = r[1], b = r[2] }
  local ok, err = pcall(C.apply_op, smp, op)
  if not ok then
    set_status("Edit failed: " .. tostring(err))
    return
  end
  S.sel_range = nil
  C.record({ op }, mode == "trim" and "Trim" or "Cut")
  C.preview_changed(true)
  set_status((mode == "trim" and "Trimmed" or "Cut") .. " the preview copy"
             .. " - loading it now uses this version (the file is untouched)")
end

-- back to the file as it is: all its steps go (one undo brings them back)
function C.undo_edits()
  local p = S.loaded_path
  local list = p and C.ops_of(p)
  if not list or #list == 0 then
    set_status("This sample has no changes")
    return
  end
  local saved = {}
  for i, op in ipairs(list) do saved[i] = op end
  local function clear() S.ops[C.file_key(p)] = {} C.reload_preview(p) end
  clear()
  C.push_undo {
    name = "Back to the file", path = p, preview = true,
    undo = function()
      local l = {}
      for i, op in ipairs(saved) do l[i] = op end
      S.ops[C.file_key(p)] = l
      C.reload_preview(p)
    end,
    redo = clear,
  }
  set_status("Back to the file as it is")
end

-- What to load for `path`: the file, or the edited copy (saved now) after
-- a trim / cut / crossfade; plus the loop and interpolation to give it
-- (nil: the defaults). A file with changes that is not in the preview is
-- put there first, so its steps are replayed.
function C.source_for(path)
  local list = C.ops_of(path)
  local here = same_path(path, S.loaded_path) and not S.wave_from_kit
  if not here and not (list and #list > 0) then return path, false, nil end
  if not here and not load_preview(path) then return path, false, nil end
  local smp = scratch_sample()
  if not smp then return path, false, nil end
  local props = { loop = C.loop_op(smp), interp = smp.interpolation_mode }
  if S.edited then
    if not (S.edit_tmp and io.exists(S.edit_tmp)) then
      local dir = C.edits_dir()
      pcall(function() if not dir_exists(dir) then os.mkdir(dir) end end)
      C.edit_n = (C.edit_n or 0) + 1
      local f = join(dir, string.format("%s (edit %d).wav",
        stem(path):gsub("[^%w%-_ %.%(%)]", "_"), C.edit_n))
      local ok = pcall(function()
        return smp.sample_buffer:save_as(f, "wav")
      end)
      if ok and io.exists(f) then S.edit_tmp = f end
    end
    if S.edit_tmp then return S.edit_tmp, true, props end
  end
  return path, false, props
end

-- give a loaded sample the loop and interpolation from C.source_for
function C.apply_props(smp, props)
  if not props then return end
  pcall(function()
    local l = props.loop
    if l then C.put_loop(smp, l.mode, l.s, l.e) end
    if props.interp then smp.interpolation_mode = props.interp end
  end)
end

-- PakettiLoadSampleBrowser.lua
-- Impulse Tracker "Load Sample" screen for Renoise: a Canvas file browser that
-- lets you navigate folders, see a highlighted file's metadata + waveform, and
-- KEYJAZZ the file on the qwerty piano keyboard WITHOUT loading it into your song.
--
-- How the "loadless preview" works: highlighting a file loads it into a single
-- hidden scratch instrument (created at the end of the instrument list). The piano
-- keys trigger that scratch instrument via trigger_instrument_note_on, so you hear
-- the file during playback without disturbing your song. Nothing touches your real
-- instruments until you CONFIRM (Enter, or press the toggle shortcut again), which
-- loads the file fresh into the smart target slot with the Paketti default template
-- and returns you to the Pattern Editor. Esc cancels and deletes the scratch
-- instrument, leaving no residue.
--
-- Keys in dialog:
--   Up/Down         move the file cursor (loads the highlighted file for preview)
--   Mod+Up/Down     any modifier (Cmd/Option/Shift/Ctrl) + Up/Down jumps to top/bottom
--   PageUp/PageDown jump a screenful
--   Enter / Return  on a folder: enter it; on a file: LOAD into target + return to Pattern Editor
--   Backspace / Left go up to the parent folder; from a Windows drive root (C:\) this
--                   goes up to a synthetic "Drives" list to hop between C:/D:/E: etc.
--   Open Folder…    button: native folder picker, reaches any folder/drive (C:/D:/E:, network)
--   Esc             cancel + unload (delete scratch instrument)
--   F1-F12          jump to folder preset N; Shift+F1-F12 stores the current folder as preset N
--   Right-Shift     "load and jam": load into the smart target slot (selected-if-empty,
--                   else first empty, else new), select it, close, turn on Edit Mode +
--                   Follow Pattern, jump to the Pattern Editor
--   Piano keys      keyjazz the highlighted file (zsxdcvgbhnjm + 23 567 9 + qwertyuiop)
--   < / >           lower / raise the keyboard (transport) octave for keyjazz
--   Space           passes through to Renoise transport (start/stop during audition)
--   Shift+Enter     load all sample files directly inside the selected folder
--   < / >           pass through to Renoise octave controls
--   Toggle shortcut confirms + closes through the same deferred action as Enter.
--
-- The folder you are in is remembered (and becomes the default next time); if it has
-- since been deleted it reverts to ~/Music/Samples. The first time you ever open the
-- dialog it asks you to pick a default folder. The highlighted file is remembered too,
-- so reopening lands you back where you were (clamped if the folder now has fewer files).

-- the file's smpl chunk defines, it is applied from our own header probe.
local function load_file_into_sample(smp, path, info)
  pcall(function() smp.loop_mode = 1 end)  -- no stale loop from before
  local loaded = smp.sample_buffer:load_from(path)
  if loaded == false or not smp.sample_buffer.has_sample_data then
    error("could not read " .. basename(path), 0)
  end
  info = info or probe_file(path)
  pcall(function()
    local n = smp.sample_buffer.number_of_frames
    if prefs.file_loops.value then
      if info and info.loop and smp.loop_mode == 1 then
        local s = clamp(info.loop.start, 1, n)
        local e = clamp(info.loop.stop, s, n)
        smp.loop_mode = info.loop.mode
        smp.loop_end = n
        smp.loop_start = s
        smp.loop_end = e
      end
    else
      smp.loop_mode = 1
    end
    if smp.loop_mode == 1 and prefs.default_loop.value > 1 then
      smp.loop_start = 1
      smp.loop_end = n
      smp.loop_mode = clamp(prefs.default_loop.value, 1, 4)
    end
  end)
  pcall(function()
    smp.interpolation_mode = clamp(prefs.default_interp.value, 1, 4)
  end)
end

-- Beats a looping sample should span at the song tempo, or nil.
-- Uses a BPM in the file name ("loop_120bpm.wav") when there is one,
-- otherwise the power of two beats closest to the song tempo.
local function sync_beats(smp, path)
  if not prefs.sync_tempo.value then return nil end
  local buf = smp.sample_buffer
  local secs = buf.number_of_frames / math.max(1, buf.sample_rate)
  if secs < 0.05 then return nil end
  local named = tonumber((basename(path or ""):lower()
                          :match("(%d%d%d?)%s*_?bpm")))
  if named and named >= 40 and named <= 300 then
    return math.max(1, math.floor(secs * named / 60 + 0.5))
  end
  local bpm = renoise.song().transport.bpm
  -- one-shots shorter than about a beat are never stretched
  if smp.loop_mode == 1 and secs < 0.9 * 60 / bpm then return nil end
  local best, best_err
  for _, n in ipairs { 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 } do
    local err = math.abs(math.log((n * 60 / secs) / bpm))
    if not best_err or err < best_err then best, best_err = n, err end
  end
  if best_err > math.log(1.5) then return nil end
  return best
end

-- Apply the browser's Beatsync setting to a sample. Used for the preview
-- and for everything that gets loaded, so what you hear is what you get.
local function apply_browser_settings(smp, path)
  pcall(function()
    local beats = sync_beats(smp, path)
    if beats then
      smp.beat_sync_lines = clamp(beats * renoise.song().transport.lpb, 1, 512)
      pcall(function() smp.beat_sync_mode = clamp(prefs.sync_mode.value, 1, 3) end)
      smp.beat_sync_enabled = true
    else
      smp.beat_sync_enabled = false
    end
  end)
end

function C.wave_frame(x)

  local w = S.wave_view and S.wave_view.width or 1

  return clamp(math.floor(clamp(x, 0, w) / math.max(1, w) * W.frames) + 1,

-- put a sample's loop exactly there (kept inside the sample)
function C.put_loop(smp, mode, ls, le)
  local n = smp.sample_buffer.number_of_frames
  ls = clamp(math.floor(ls), 1, n)
  le = clamp(math.floor(le), ls, n)
  smp.loop_mode = 1
  smp.loop_start = 1
  smp.loop_end = le
  smp.loop_start = ls
  smp.loop_mode = clamp(mode, 1, 4)
end

-- trim to / cut out frames a..b of a sample's audio (the loop moves along)
function C.edit_data(smp, mode, a, b)
  local buf = smp.sample_buffer
  local n, chs = buf.number_of_frames, buf.number_of_channels
  a, b = clamp(a, 1, n), clamp(b, 1, n)
  local keep = (mode == "trim") and { { a, b } } or { { 1, a - 1 }, { b + 1, n } }
  local total = 0
  for _, k in ipairs(keep) do total = total + math.max(0, k[2] - k[1] + 1) end
  if total < 2 then error("nothing would be left", 0) end
  -- where a frame of the old sample ends up
  local function moved(f)
    if mode == "trim" then return clamp(f - a + 1, 1, total) end
    if f < a then return f end
    if f > b then return f - (b - a + 1) end
    return clamp(a, 1, total)
  end
  local data = {}
  for c = 1, chs do
    local t, i = {}, 0
    for _, k in ipairs(keep) do
      for f = k[1], k[2] do i = i + 1 t[i] = buf:sample_data(c, f) end
    end
    data[c] = t
  end
  local rate, bits = buf.sample_rate, buf.bit_depth
  local lm, ls, le = smp.loop_mode, smp.loop_start, smp.loop_end
  local interp = smp.interpolation_mode
  if not buf:create_sample_data(rate, bits, chs, total) then
    error("could not make the new sample", 0)
  end
  buf:prepare_sample_data_changes(false)   -- the preview needs no undo
  for c = 1, chs do
    local t = data[c]
    for f = 1, total do buf:set_sample_data(c, f, t[f]) end
  end
  buf:finalize_sample_data_changes()
  local nls, nle = moved(ls), moved(le)
  C.put_loop(smp, nle > nls and lm or 1, nls, math.max(nls, nle))
  pcall(function() smp.interpolation_mode = interp end)
end

-- equal-power crossfade over `len` frames at the loop (see below)
function C.xfade_data(smp, len)
  local buf = smp.sample_buffer
  local ls, le = smp.loop_start, smp.loop_end
  len = math.min(len, ls - 1, le - ls)
  if len < 2 then error("needs audio before the loop start", 0) end
  local half_pi = math.pi / 2
  local sin, cos = math.sin, math.cos
  buf:prepare_sample_data_changes(false)
  for c = 1, buf.number_of_channels do
    for k = 1, len do
      local t = k / len
      local dst = le - len + k            -- end of the loop, fading out
      local src = ls - len + k - 1        -- before the start, fading in
      buf:set_sample_data(c, dst,
        buf:sample_data(c, dst) * cos(t * half_pi)
        + buf:sample_data(c, src) * sin(t * half_pi))
    end
  end
  buf:finalize_sample_data_changes()
end

-- one step on a sample
function C.apply_op(smp, op)
  if op.t == "loop" then C.put_loop(smp, op.mode, op.s, op.e)
  elseif op.t == "interp" then smp.interpolation_mode = clamp(op.mode, 1, 4)
  elseif op.t == "trim" or op.t == "cut" then C.edit_data(smp, op.t, op.a, op.b)
  elseif op.t == "xfade" then
    if op.ls then C.put_loop(smp, op.mode, op.ls, op.le) end  -- its loop
    C.xfade_data(smp, op.len)
  end
end

-- the loop of a sample as a step
function C.loop_op(smp)
  return { t = "loop", mode = smp.loop_mode, s = smp.loop_start, e = smp.loop_end }

function C.edit_preview(mode)
  C.quiet()
  local r = S.sel_range
  local smp = C.preview_smp()
  if not r or not smp then
    set_status("Drag across the waveform to select a part first")
    return
  end
  release_all()
  clear_preview_slices()
  local op = { t = mode, a = r[1], b = r[2] }
  local ok, err = pcall(C.apply_op, smp, op)

    return
  end
  S.sel_range = nil
  C.record({ op }, mode == "trim" and "Trim" or "Cut")
  C.preview_changed(true)
  set_status((mode == "trim" and "Trimmed" or "Cut") .. " the preview copy"
             .. " - loading it now uses this version (the file is untouched)")
end

-- back to the file as it is: all its steps go (one undo brings them back)
function C.undo_edits()
  local p = S.loaded_path
  local list = p and C.ops_of(p)
  if not list or #list == 0 then
    set_status("This sample has no changes")
    return
  end
  local saved = {}
  for i, op in ipairs(list) do saved[i] = op end
  local function clear() S.ops[C.file_key(p)] = {} C.reload_preview(p) end
  clear()
  C.push_undo {
    name = "Back to the file", path = p, preview = true,
    undo = function()
      local l = {}
      for i, op in ipairs(saved) do l[i] = op end
      S.ops[C.file_key(p)] = l
      C.reload_preview(p)
    end,
    redo = clear,
  }
  set_status("Back to the file as it is")
end

-- What to load for `path`: the file, or the edited copy (saved now) after
-- a trim / cut / crossfade; plus the loop and interpolation to give it
-- (nil: the defaults). A file with changes that is not in the preview is
-- put there first, so its steps are replayed.
function C.source_for(path)
  local list = C.ops_of(path)
  local here = same_path(path, S.loaded_path) and not S.wave_from_kit
  if not here and not (list and #list > 0) then return path, false, nil end
  if not here and not load_preview(path) then return path, false, nil end
  local smp = scratch_sample()
  if not smp then return path, false, nil end
  local props = { loop = C.loop_op(smp), interp = smp.interpolation_mode }
  if S.edited then
    if not (S.edit_tmp and io.exists(S.edit_tmp)) then
      local dir = C.edits_dir()
      pcall(function() if not dir_exists(dir) then os.mkdir(dir) end end)
      C.edit_n = (C.edit_n or 0) + 1
      local f = join(dir, string.format("%s (edit %d).wav",
        stem(path):gsub("[^%w%-_ %.%(%)]", "_"), C.edit_n))
      local ok = pcall(function()
        return smp.sample_buffer:save_as(f, "wav")
      end)
      if ok and io.exists(f) then S.edit_tmp = f end
    end
    if S.edit_tmp then return S.edit_tmp, true, props end
  end
  return path, false, props
end

-- give a loaded sample the loop and interpolation from C.source_for
function C.apply_props(smp, props)
  if not props then return end
  pcall(function()
    local l = props.loop
    if l then C.put_loop(smp, l.mode, l.s, l.e) end
    if props.interp then smp.interpolation_mode = props.interp end
  end)
end

-- PakettiLoadSampleBrowser.lua
-- Impulse Tracker "Load Sample" screen for Renoise: a Canvas file browser that
-- lets you navigate folders, see a highlighted file's metadata + waveform, and
-- KEYJAZZ the file on the qwerty piano keyboard WITHOUT loading it into your song.
--
-- How the "loadless preview" works: highlighting a file loads it into a single

-- Beats a looping sample should span at the song tempo, or nil.
-- Uses a BPM in the file name ("loop_120bpm.wav") when there is one,
-- otherwise the power of two beats closest to the song tempo.
local function sync_beats(smp, path)
  if not prefs.sync_tempo.value then return nil end
  local buf = smp.sample_buffer
  local secs = buf.number_of_frames / math.max(1, buf.sample_rate)
  if secs < 0.05 then return nil end
  local named = tonumber((basename(path or ""):lower()
                          :match("(%d%d%d?)%s*_?bpm")))
  if named and named >= 40 and named <= 300 then
    return math.max(1, math.floor(secs * named / 60 + 0.5))
  end
  local bpm = renoise.song().transport.bpm
  -- one-shots shorter than about a beat are never stretched
  if smp.loop_mode == 1 and secs < 0.9 * 60 / bpm then return nil end
  local best, best_err
  for _, n in ipairs { 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 } do
    local err = math.abs(math.log((n * 60 / secs) / bpm))
    if not best_err or err < best_err then best, best_err = n, err end
  end
  if best_err > math.log(1.5) then return nil end
  return best
end

function C.edit_data(smp, mode, a, b)
  local buf = smp.sample_buffer
  local n, chs = buf.number_of_frames, buf.number_of_channels
  a, b = clamp(a, 1, n), clamp(b, 1, n)
  local keep = (mode == "trim") and { { a, b } } or { { 1, a - 1 }, { b + 1, n } }
  local total = 0

    if f < a then return f end
    if f > b then return f - (b - a + 1) end
    return clamp(a, 1, total)
  end
  local data = {}
  for c = 1, chs do
    local t, i = {}, 0
    for _, k in ipairs(keep) do
      for f = k[1], k[2] do i = i + 1 t[i] = buf:sample_data(c, f) end
    end
    data[c] = t

  local rate, bits = buf.sample_rate, buf.bit_depth
  local lm, ls, le = smp.loop_mode, smp.loop_start, smp.loop_end
  local interp = smp.interpolation_mode
  if not buf:create_sample_data(rate, bits, chs, total) then
    error("could not make the new sample", 0)
  end
  buf:prepare_sample_data_changes(false)   -- the preview needs no undo
  for c = 1, chs do
    local t = data[c]
    for f = 1, total do buf:set_sample_data(c, f, t[f]) end

  buf:finalize_sample_data_changes()
  local nls, nle = moved(ls), moved(le)

end

function C.xfade_data(smp, len)
  local buf = smp.sample_buffer
  local ls, le = smp.loop_start, smp.loop_end
  len = math.min(len, ls - 1, le - ls)
  if len < 2 then error("needs audio before the loop start", 0) end
  local half_pi = math.pi / 2
  local sin, cos = math.sin, math.cos
  buf:prepare_sample_data_changes(false)
  for c = 1, buf.number_of_channels do
    for k = 1, len do
      local t = k / len
      local dst = le - len + k            -- end of the loop, fading out
      local src = ls - len + k - 1        -- before the start, fading in
      buf:set_sample_data(c, dst,
        buf:sample_data(c, dst) * cos(t * half_pi)
        + buf:sample_data(c, src) * sin(t * half_pi))
    end
  end
  buf:finalize_sample_data_changes()
end

-- PakettiLoadSampleBrowser.lua
-- Impulse Tracker "Load Sample" screen for Renoise: a Canvas file browser that
-- lets you navigate folders, see a highlighted file's metadata + waveform, and
-- KEYJAZZ the file on the qwerty piano keyboard WITHOUT loading it into your song.
--
-- How the "loadless preview" works: highlighting a file loads it into a single
-- hidden scratch instrument (created at the end of the instrument list). The piano
-- keys trigger that scratch instrument via trigger_instrument_note_on, so you hear
-- the file during playback without disturbing your song. Nothing touches your real
-- instruments until you CONFIRM (Enter, or press the toggle shortcut again), which
-- loads the file fresh into the smart target slot with the Paketti default template
-- and returns you to the Pattern Editor. Esc cancels and deletes the scratch
-- instrument, leaving no residue.
--
-- Keys in dialog:
--   Up/Down         move the file cursor (loads the highlighted file for preview)
--   Mod+Up/Down     any modifier (Cmd/Option/Shift/Ctrl) + Up/Down jumps to top/bottom
--   PageUp/PageDown jump a screenful
--   Enter / Return  on a folder: enter it; on a file: LOAD into target + return to Pattern Editor
--   Backspace / Left go up to the parent folder; from a Windows drive root (C:\) this
--                   goes up to a synthetic "Drives" list to hop between C:/D:/E: etc.
--   Open Folder…    button: native folder picker, reaches any folder/drive (C:/D:/E:, network)
--   Esc             cancel + unload (delete scratch instrument)
--   F1-F12          jump to folder preset N; Shift+F1-F12 stores the current folder as preset N
--   Right-Shift     "load and jam": load into the smart target slot (selected-if-empty,
--                   else first empty, else new), select it, close, turn on Edit Mode +
--                   Follow Pattern, jump to the Pattern Editor
--   Piano keys      keyjazz the highlighted file (zsxdcvgbhnjm + 23 567 9 + qwertyuiop)
--   < / >           lower / raise the keyboard (transport) octave for keyjazz
--   Space           passes through to Renoise transport (start/stop during audition)
--   Shift+Enter     load all sample files directly inside the selected folder
--   < / >           pass through to Renoise octave controls
--   Toggle shortcut confirms + closes through the same deferred action as Enter.
--
-- The folder you are in is remembered (and becomes the default next time); if it has
-- since been deleted it reverts to ~/Music/Samples. The first time you ever open the
-- dialog it asks you to pick a default folder. The highlighted file is remembered too,
-- so reopening lands you back where you were (clamped if the folder now has fewer files).

  [","] = 12, l = 13, ["."] = 14, ["ö"] = 15, ["-"] = 16, ["ä"] = 17,
}

local PLSB_UPPER = {
  q = 0, ["2"] = 1, w = 2, ["3"] = 3, e = 4, r = 5, ["5"] = 6, t = 7, ["6"] = 8,
  y = 9, ["7"] = 10, u = 11, i = 12, ["9"] = 13, o = 14, ["0"] = 15, p = 16,
  ["å"] = 17, ["´"] = 18, ["¨"] = 18,
}

  raw=true, snd=true, caf=true, au=true, wv=true, voc=true, w64=true, aifc=true }
"}

text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"mkdir -p manual
cat > manual/KeyjazzBrowserComparison.md <<'EOF'
# Paketti Keyjazz loader versus SimpleBrowser 1.2.0

Compared the current PakettiLoadSampleBrowser.lua working tree against main.lua extracted from /Users/esaruoho/Downloads/com.phaos.SimpleBrowser.xrnx. This is a source inspection, not a live comparative Renoise test.

Both use a scratch instrument for auditioning, support keyboard piano playback, waveform selections and loop editing, and can import edited preview audio while leaving the source audio file untouched.

| Area | Paketti Keyjazz loader | Phaos SimpleBrowser 1.2.0 |
|---|---|---|
| Main purpose | Audition, then load with the Paketti template and return to the tracker | Browse, edit and build multisample instruments in a persistent browser |
| Layout | One folder/file list, metadata and waveform | One or two browsing panes, optional multisample panel, waveform/playhead and controls |
| Loading target | Selected empty instrument, first empty instrument, or a new one | New instrument, replace selected sample, or add to multisample instrument |
| Folder imports | Shift-Enter: direct files into separate instruments | Folder/sample selections can build a multisample instrument; optional recursive traversal |
| Formats | Native audio plus Paketti expansion/importers for formats such as REX, ITI, SF2 and EXS; non-native formats lack live preview | Audio extension list: WAV, AIF/AIFF, FLAC, MP3, OGG |
| WAV cues | Shared embedded-cue importer; zero/one cue stays unsliced; active preview loop overrides slicing | Normal sample loading plus WAV smpl loop probing; no dedicated cue-to-slice import found |
| Loop editing | Mode cycling, flag dragging, Selection to Loop | Those functions plus zero-crossing snapping and loop crossfade |
| Audio editing | Cmd-X removes selected frames; edited audio survives final native loading | Cut, trim, loop crossfade, reset to original |
| Edit history | No browser undo/redo; switching files resets edits | Per-file operation lists retained while browsing, browser undo/redo |
| Playback settings | Interpolation, oversampling, autofade controls for current preview; chosen values survive loading | Interpolation and tempo sync controls; prehear volume/output controls. Autofade and oversampling occur in snapshot properties, but no dedicated controls found |
| Multisample mapping | No dedicated kit panel in this browser | Drumkit, Distribute, Layer; white-key mapping and overlap modes |
| Search | Current-directory name filter: words, alternatives, exclusions, phrases, wildcards | Similar query syntax plus root-wide/recursive search options |
| Locations | Twelve F-key presets, last folder/file remembered, folder picker | Eight bookmarks, extra folder places, hidden entries, rescan and reveal in file browser |
| Delete | Cmd-Backspace confirms actual source-file deletion; retains/clamps row | Hide source entries and remove instrument samples; no actual source-file deletion action found |
| Tracker integration | Confirm closes browser; Right-Shift loads a new instrument and enables Edit Mode/Follow Pattern | Load-and-write-note action and multisample row note insertion; browser keeps broader editing workflow |
| Caps Lock | Angle-key octave handling ignores Caps Lock | Caps Lock toggles keyboard controls mode |

Compared the supplied **SimpleBrowser 1.2.0** code with Paketti’s current loader.

| Feature | Paketti Keyjazz | SimpleBrowser |
|---|---|---|
| Loading | Paketti template, smart empty target, load-and-jam | New instrument, replace sample, add to multisample |
| Formats | Broader Paketti importers, including REX/SF2/EXS | WAV, AIFF, FLAC, MP3, OGG |
| Preview edits | Cut selection, adjust loops | Cut, trim, crossfade, zero-crossing snapping |
| Remember edits when browsing | **Switching files discards edits** | Keeps per-file edits |
| Undo/redo | No browser history | Browser history |
| Playback controls | Interpolation, oversampling, autofade | Interpolation, beatsync, preview volume/output |
| Multisample building | No integrated panel | Drumkit, Distribute, Layer |
| Search | Current folder | Recursive/root-wide options |
| File deletion | Confirmed deletion; cursor retained | Hide entries; remove instrument samples |

**SimpleBrowser currently has the richer editing workflow.** Paketti’s strengths are its template integration, broader formats, WAV cue handling, and immediate tracker workflow.

The biggest gap is **keeping edits when switching files**, followed by undo/redo, trim, crossfade, and snapping.

from pathlib import Path
p=Path('manual/KeyjazzBrowserComparison.md');s=p.read_text().replace('Cut selection, adjust loops | Cut','Cut and trim selection, adjust loops | Cut').replace('Interpolation, oversampling, autofade controls for current preview; chosen values survive loading','Interpolation, oversampling, autofade, preview volume and tempo sync; chosen playback values survive loading').replace('Current-directory name filter: words, alternatives, exclusions, phrases, wildcards','Recursive opening/chosen-root search: words, alternatives, exclusions, phrases, wildcards').replace('The largest remaining differences are retained per-file edits, undo/redo, trim, crossfade, zero-crossing snapping, tempo sync, multisample assembly and recursive search.','The largest remaining differences are retained per-file edits, undo/redo, crossfade, zero-crossing snapping, multisample assembly, preview output routing and a moving playhead.');s+='''
## Remaining gaps after the added controls

1. Per-file edit retention: navigating away currently discards Paketti cuts, trims, loop edits and explicit playback choices. SimpleBrowser keeps operation lists keyed by file while the browser is open.
2. Browser undo/redo and reset-to-original: SimpleBrowser covers preview edits, settings, multisample changes and loads. Paketti has no equivalent browser history.
3. Loop crossfade and zero-crossing snapping are not integrated into Paketti's browser (separate Paketti tools do not make them browser features).
4. Multisample panel: assemble/remove/reorder samples; Drumkit, Distribute and Layer mapping; white-key mapping; overlap Play All/Cycle/Random; audition the assembled instrument.
5. Shift-click/Shift-arrow multiple-file selection and selected-group loading.
6. Two-pane folder/sample layout, pane focus switching and keyboard control-navigation mode.
7. Automatic prehear on selection, moving playback cursor and explicit Master versus selected-track prehear routing.
8. Replace selected sample, load-and-write-note, and instrument/sample-slot navigation within the browser.
9. Hide/unhide entries, reveal in Finder, extra root places, explicit rescan and in-dialog help.
10. Tempo inference from BPM filenames: SimpleBrowser uses a filename BPM when present, then nearest power-of-two beat inference with a plausibility guard; Paketti currently always chooses nearest power-of-two beats.

Suggested implementation order based on protecting edits first: retain per-file edits, undo/redo, reset-to-original; then crossfade and snapping; then preview playhead/routing/autoplay; then multisample and navigation features.
''';p.write_text(s)

function C.set_interp(mode)
  prefs.default_interp.value = clamp(mode, 1, #C.INTERP_ITEMS)
  set_status("Interpolation: " .. C.INTERP_ITEMS[prefs.default_interp.value])

-- right-click on the waveform
function C.wave_menu()
  local has_sel = S.sel_range ~= nil and not S.wave_from_kit
  local smp = C.preview_smp()
  local items = {
    { name = "Play from selection", active = has_sel, invoke = function()
        local W = S.wave
        if W and S.sel_range then
          play_from((S.sel_range[1] - 1) / W.frames)
        end
      end },
    { name = "Set loop to selection   (Ctrl-Shift-L)", active = has_sel,
      invoke = function() C.loop_to_selection() end },
    { name = (has_sel and "Loop selection and crossfade" or "Crossfade loop"),
      active = C.xfade_possible(),
      invoke = function() C.do_xfade() end },
    { name = "---Trim to selection", active = has_sel,
      invoke = function() C.edit_preview("trim") end },
    { name = "Cut selection", active = has_sel,
      invoke = function() C.edit_preview("cut") end },
  }
  items[#items + 1] = { name = "---Snap loop points to zero crossings",
    selected = prefs.snap_zero.value, invoke = function() C.toggle_snap() end }
  items[#items + 1] = { name = "---Back to the file (undo all changes)",
    active = S.loaded_path ~= nil and #(C.ops_of(S.loaded_path) or {}) > 0,
    invoke = C.undo_edits }
  pcall(function() renoise.app():show_menu(S.dialog, items) end)
end

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Loop points and loop crossfade
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Loop points move by keyboard (controls mode) or by dragging their flags
-- on the waveform, snapping to zero crossings (an option). The crossfade
-- is an equal-power blend, inspired by afta8's "xfade pow": the audio before

The main remaining gaps are:

- **Keep edits when switching files** — Paketti currently discards cuts, trims and loop changes when you browse away.
- **Undo/redo**, plus **Reset to Original**.
- **Loop crossfade** and **zero-crossing snapping**.
- **Moving playback cursor**, automatic audition on selection, and Master/selected-track preview routing.
- **Multisample panel**: assemble, reorder and map samples as Drumkit, Distribute or Layer.
- **Multiple-file selection** with Shift-click/arrows.
- **Replace selected sample** while preserving its mappings/envelopes.
- **Load and write a note** at the pattern cursor.
- **Two-pane browsing** and keyboard navigation between controls.
- Hide/unhide, reveal in Finder, extra folder locations and built-in help.
- **BPM-from-filename beatsync**; Paketti currently estimates the nearest beat length.

I’d prioritize **retaining per-file edits → undo/redo → reset**, then **crossfade and snapping**.

local function plsb_wave_render(ctx)
  ctx:clear_rect(0, 0, WAVE_W, WAVE_H)
  ctx.fill_color = COL_BG
  ctx:begin_path(); ctx:rect(0, 0, WAVE_W, WAVE_H); ctx:fill()
  ctx.stroke_color = COL_FRAME
  ctx.line_width = 1
  ctx:begin_path(); ctx:rect(0, 0, WAVE_W, WAVE_H); ctx:stroke()

  if not (S.peaks and S.preview_ok) then return end
  local lanes = math.min(#S.peaks, 2)
  if lanes < 1 then return end
  local lane_h = WAVE_H / lanes
  for ch = 1, lanes do
    local base = (ch - 1) * lane_h + lane_h / 2
    -- zero line
    ctx.stroke_color = COL_ZERO
    ctx:begin_path(); ctx:move_to(0, base); ctx:line_to(WAVE_W, base); ctx:stroke()
    -- peaks
    local col = S.peaks[ch]
    local pw = #col
    ctx.stroke_color = COL_WAVE
    ctx:begin_path()
    for px = 1, pw do
      local x = (px - 1) * (WAVE_W / pw)
      local mn = col[px][1]
      local mx = col[px][2]
      ctx:move_to(x, base - mx * (lane_h / 2 - 2))
      ctx:line_to(x, base - mn * (lane_h / 2 - 2))
    end
    ctx:stroke()
  end

  -- frames->x in this canvas (inlined; the shared helper is defined further down)
  local frames = (S.loop and S.loop.frames) or S.meta.frames or 1
  if frames < 1 then frames = 1 end
  local function fx(f) return (f - 1) / frames * WAVE_W end

  -- drag-selection band
  if S.sel_range then
    local a = math.min(S.sel_range[1], S.sel_range[2])
    local b = math.max(S.sel_range[1], S.sel_range[2])
    local x1 = fx(a)
    local x2 = fx(b)
    ctx.fill_color = { 232, 232, 214, 70 }   -- translucent cream
    ctx:begin_path(); ctx:rect(x1, 0, math.max(1, x2 - x1), WAVE_H); ctx:fill()
  end

  -- loop markers (start/end lines + small flags, like the sample editor)
  if S.loop and S.loop.mode and S.loop.mode ~= renoise.Sample.LOOP_MODE_OFF then
    local xs = fx(S.loop.start)
    local xe = fx(S.loop.stop)
    ctx.fill_color = { 255, 190, 60, 255 }   -- amber loop flags/lines
    ctx:begin_path(); ctx:rect(xs, 0, 1, WAVE_H); ctx:fill()

  end
  S.playhead_timer = callback
  renoise.tool():add_timer(callback, 30)
  if S.vb and S.wave_id and S.vb.views[S.wave_id] then S.vb.views[S.wave_id]:update() end
end

local playhead=assert(source:match('(local function plsb_stop_playhead%(%).-)\n%-%- scratch instrument'))
renoise.Sample={LOOP_MODE_OFF=1,LOOP_MODE_FORWARD=2,LOOP_MODE_REVERSE=3,LOOP_MODE_PING_PONG=4}
local phstate={scratch_index=1,dialog={visible=true}}
local phsample={sample_buffer={has_sample_data=true,number_of_frames=1000,sample_rate=100},sample_mapping={base_note=48},transpose=0,fine_tune=0,loop_mode=4,loop_start=200,loop_end=400,beat_sync_enabled=false}
renoise.song=function() return {instruments={{samples={phsample}}},transport={bpm=120,lpb=4}} end
local stop,pos,start=assert(load('local S=...\n'..playhead..'\nreturn plsb_stop_playhead,plsb_playhead_position,plsb_start_playhead'))(phstate)
local p={offset=300,speed=100,frames=1000,mode=1,start=200,stop=400}
assert(pos(p,2)==500 and pos(p,8)==nil)
p.offset=1; p.mode=2; assert(pos(p,5)==301)
p.mode=3; assert(pos(p,5)==299)
p.mode=4; assert(pos(p,5)==299 and pos(p,7)==301)
start('__wave__',48,300); assert(phstate.playhead_frame==300 and phstate.playhead.mode==1)
stop(); assert(not phstate.playhead and not next(timers))
start('z',60); assert(phstate.playhead.speed==200 and phstate.playhead.mode==4)
phstate.dialog.visible=false; next(timers)(); assert(not phstate.playhead and not next(timers))
print('sample-browser-playhead: passed')
EOF
lua tests/sample-browser-editing.lua
lua tests/sample-browser-loop-load.lua
